content: The associations between physical activity (PA) and various health outcomes were evaluated across multiple studies, with findings summarized as follows: 1. HDL Cholesterol: Favorable associations were observed in 2 out of 5 studies (Chaput et al., 2013; Hjorth et al., 2014a). Null associations were reported in 3 out of 5 studies (Andersen et al., 2006; Hurtig-Wennlof et al., 2007; Owen et al., 2010). 2. Vigorous Physical Activity (VPA) and HDL Cholesterol: Null associations were reported in 1 out of 1 study (Stabelini Neto et al., 2014). 3. Moderate-to-Vigorous Physical Activity (MVPA) and High Risk Cholesterol: Increased MVPA was associated with reduced odds of high risk cholesterol in 1 out of 1 study (LeBlanc and Janssen, 2010). 4. Total Cholesterol: Favorable associations were observed in 1 out of 3 studies (Hurtig-Wennlof et al., 2007). Null associations were reported in 2 out of 3 studies (Hurtig-Wennlof et al., 2007; Mendoza et al., 2012). 5. Non-HDL Cholesterol: Favorable associations with MVPA (total, bouts, sporadic) were reported in 1 out of 1 study (Holman et al., 2011). 6. LDL Cholesterol: Null associations were reported in 3 out of 3 studies (LeBlanc and Janssen, 2010; Mendoza et al., 2012; Carson et al., 2013). 7. Insulin Resistance (HOMA): Favorable associations were observed in 5 out of 6 studies (Andersen et al., 2006; Rizzo et al., 2008; Sardinha et al., 2008; Owen et al., 2010; Hjorth et al., 2014a). Null associations were reported in 1 out of 6 studies (Jimenez-Pavon et al., 2013c). 8. Fasting Insulin: Favorable associations were observed in 8 out of 11 studies (Brage et al., 2004a; Andersen et al., 2006; Ekelund et al., 2006; Butte et al., 2007b; Rizzo et al., 2008; Sardinha et al., 2008; Owen et al., 2010; Jimenez-Pavon et al., 2012). Null associations were reported in 1 out of 11 studies (Jimenez-Pavon et al., 2013c). Mixed associations (favorable and null) were reported in 2 out of 11 studies (Wennlof et al., 2005; Hurtig-Wennlof et al., 2007). 9. Fasting Glucose: Favorable associations were observed in 3 out of 7 studies (Andersen et al., 2006; Ekelund et al., 2006; Rizzo et al., 2008). Null associations were reported in 3 out of 7 studies (Brage et al., 2004a; Chaput et al., 2013; Jimenez-Pavon et al., 2013c). Mixed associations (favorable and null) were reported in 1 out of 7 studies (Hurtig-Wennlof et al., 2007). 10. HbA1c: Null associations were reported in 1 out of 1 study (Owen et al., 2010). 11. Inflammatory Markers (CRP, TNF-α, IL-6, C3, C4): Null associations were reported between meeting PA guidelines and CRP in 1 out of 1 study (Loprinzi et al., 2013). Null associations were also reported for IL-6, TNF-α, C3, or C4 in 1 out of 1 study (Martinez-Gomez et al., 2012). 12. Artery Properties: Total PA was negatively associated with pulse wave velocity (PWV) in 1 out of 1 study (Sakuragi et al., 2009). Null associations were reported with carotid intima-media thickness (IMT) in 1 out of 1 study (Lamotte et al., 2013). 13. Cardiac Sympathetic/Parasympathetic Modulation: MVPA was positively associated with one index of cardiac parasympathetic modulation (root mean square of successive differences) but not associated with another (high-frequency power). It was negatively associated with sympathetic-parasympathetic balance in 1 out of 1 study (Gutin et al., 2005b). 14. Composite Cardiometabolic Disease Risk Score: Meeting PA guidelines was associated with reduced cardiometabolic risk scores in 2 out of 2 studies (Mendoza et al., 2012; Janssen et al., 2013). 15. Homocysteine: Null associations were reported for total PA, MVPA, VPA, or MPA in 1 out of 1 study (Ruiz et al., 2007). These findings highlight the variability in the associations between physical activity and health outcomes, with some studies showing favorable effects, others showing null effects, and a few reporting mixed results.
